name: text_mode_full_journey
description: The real product path: only the patient speaks and every Daphne reply is produced by the decision engine. Hesitation must block the booking, the engine must ask for a day/time before acting, and the booking must land once both are satisfied. Also asserts that authored clinical wording reaches the patient verbatim. The final turn ('Wednesday afternoon works for me') deliberately pairs a day/time with an affirmation phrase -- the parsing itself is pinned down by a deterministic unit check (scripts/test_preference.mjs), not asserted here, since whether this mock calendar's slots happen to fall on a Wednesday depends on the real date the suite runs on.

turns.content: My doctor keeps bringing up a colonoscopy and honestly I keep putting it off.
No, never. I've never had a colonoscopy or any of those stool tests.
My father had colon cancer. He was 52 when they found it.
Nothing on my mom's side that I know of.
No bleeding, no weight loss, nothing like that at all.
I don't know. My sister said the prep was horrible and I'm nervous about the sedation.
Okay, you've talked me into it. Please go ahead and book it.
My husband Mark can pick me up, his cell is 555-201-3344.
Wait, what day was that appointment again?

turns.expectReplyNotContains: Anything else I can help with
